question: Can a fixed many-to-one character decoder recover new hidden Latin controls that lie outside the bijective family?
scope: Known Latin, normalized 2000-letter controls. No Voynich translation or language identification. No Kraken retraining.

presentations: one new bijective encryption per content
one shuffled homophonic ciphertext per content

search.baseline: unchanged stage86 C++ core at base commit
search.expanded: 26 cipher symbols independently map to any of 26 plaintext letters; single-symbol reassignment and swaps
search.selection: maximum integer4gram language-model score per case; lexicographic key tie-break
search.budget_note: same annealing proposal counts, different neighborhoods and polish costs; not equal compute

primary_gate.many_to_one_homophonic: all 3 content streams exact for all 2000 letters and all observed symbol assignments; absent mappings excluded
primary_gate.nulls: descriptive; no abstention threshold or null-detection claim

by_case: candidate and gold integer LM scores
evaluation.baseline_homophonic_ceiling: sum over plaintext letters of maximum frequency among disjoint cipher aliases / 2000
objective_diagnostics: gold outside family for bijective homophonic cases
representable gold outranks candidate: search shortfall
candidate outranks different gold: objective misranking
different candidates with equal gold score: objective tie
evaluation.paired_comparisons: 3 contents; paired mono/homo are correlated, not six independent trials

chronology: publish frozen source, public inputs, opaque commitments before search
run GitHub Actions with public inputs only
publish full predictions before authorizing reveal
preserve failures; no case replacement or solver retuning
execution_environment: Local executor unavailable; run computations in GitHub Actions, archive logs/artifacts and commit outputs
interpretation_limit: Successful Latin control recovery cannot establish a Voynich key, language, homophony or meaning.
